Requirement: Lawful basis identified and documented for every processing purpose
Evidence: Draft Privacy Policy lists purposes and bases; consent records for recording and marketing (consents table, E2E tested)
Gaps: Bases not validated by a specialist; records of processing not written
Responsible role: Data controller (Academy Owner) with DPO/privacy adviser
Corrective action: Validate bases; complete Record of Processing Activities

Requirement: Record of Processing Activities (RoPA)
Applicability: Yes — processing is not occasional, so the under-250-employees exemption does not apply
Gaps: No RoPA
Corrective action: Prepare RoPA (purposes, categories, recipients, transfers, retention, security measures)

Requirement: Transparent privacy information to learners
Evidence: /privacy page (draft) covers identity, purposes, recipients, transfers, rights, recordings
Gaps: Legal entity, contact, retention periods and processor list are placeholders; not legally reviewed
Corrective action: Complete placeholders; legal review; publish version history

Requirement: Data subject rights: access, portability, erasure, rectification, objection
Evidence: Self-service JSON export and deletion request (E2E tested); profile editing; RLS-protected
Gaps: No staff workflow or deadline tracking for deletion requests; export does not yet cover learning records (progress, quiz, submissions, workshop logs)
Corrective action: Extend export to all learner data; build request-handling workflow with one-month response deadline

Requirement: Data Protection Impact Assessment before processing recordings and AI-generated feedback
Source: GDPR Art. 35; UODO list of processing operations requiring a DPIA
Applicability: Likely yes — innovative technology, evaluation of individuals, voice and video
Gaps: No DPIA
Corrective action: Carry out a DPIA before Phase 4 goes live

Requirement: Data processing agreements with all processors
Applicability: Yes (Supabase, Vercel, email provider, AI provider, analytics; Stripe partly as an independent controller)
Gaps: No DPAs signed (providers not yet contracted)
Corrective action: Accept and file each provider's DPA; keep a processor register

Requirement: International transfer safeguards
Applicability: Yes if US providers are used (AI, hosting, email)
Evidence: Privacy Policy draft mentions SCCs
Gaps: Transfer mechanisms per provider not documented (EU–US Data Privacy Framework certification or SCCs; transfer impact assessment)
Corrective action: Document the mechanism for each provider; choose EU data regions where available

Requirement: Retention periods defined and enforced
Gaps: Retention periods are placeholders; no automated deletion
Corrective action: Adopt a Data Retention Schedule; implement scheduled deletion (recordings, inactive accounts, logs)

Requirement: Personal data breach notification (72 hours to the authority; affected individuals when high risk)
Gaps: No breach procedure, no breach register
Corrective action: Adopt an Incident and Data Breach Response Procedure and a breach register

Requirement: Data protection by design and by default
Evidence: Data minimisation in profile (no date of birth or health data); RLS on all 15 tables; least privilege for anonymous users; no service-role key in the app; consent toggles off by default
Gaps: Teaching staff can read all learners' progress (not only assigned cohorts); no retention automation
Corrective action: Restrict staff access to assigned cohorts; implement retention

Requirement: No solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects
Evidence: Code review 26 Nov 2026: no AI or automated scoring exists; lesson completion depends only on the learner's own actions; no certificate issuance is implemented; the approved product rule requires human assessor approval for certificates
Gaps: Must be maintained when AI feedback is introduced in Phase 4
Corrective action: Keep AI output advisory; re-verify in the Phase 4 audit

Requirement: Data Protection Officer appointment (or documented decision not to appoint)
Applicability: Probably not mandatory (no large-scale special-category processing or large-scale systematic monitoring), but the decision must be documented
Gaps: No documented DPO decision
Corrective action: Document the decision; consider an external privacy adviser

Requirement: Special-category data not processed unnecessarily (health, biometrics)
Evidence: No health fields collected; recordings are not used for identification (therefore not biometric data in the GDPR sense); Terms and FAQ prohibit patient data
Gaps: Learners may disclose their own health information (e.g. anxiety, stammering) in free text; no guidance at input points
Corrective action: Add guidance at free-text inputs; never use voice for identification

Requirement: No patient-identifiable or confidential clinical data in learner submissions
Type: Legally mandatory (for learners as data controllers of patient data) / platform safeguard
Evidence: Terms, Privacy Policy, FAQ, contact form, exercises and assignments include explicit warnings; examples are fictional and composite
Gaps: No technical detection; no process for removing content that is reported
Corrective action: Add a reporting and removal procedure; consider a warning at submission

Requirement: Adult learners only; age confirmation
Applicability: Yes (programme is for qualified and training doctors)
Evidence: Sign-up requires acceptance of the Terms (required checkbox), and the Terms draft states that users must be at least 18
Gaps: No explicit age or professional-status confirmation; Terms not reviewed
Corrective action: Add explicit age confirmation at sign-up and checkout

Requirement: Prohibition of emotion recognition in education (AI must not infer learners' emotions)
Source: EU AI Act Art. 5(1)(f); applicable since 2 Feb 2025
Evidence: Code review 26 Nov 2026: no AI, camera or voice analysis exists in the platform; approved design limits feedback to observable communication behaviours; requirement written into AI governance requirements (AUDIT_REPORT §3)
Gaps: Must be enforced in AI prompts, features and vendor selection (no 'nervousness' or 'confidence' detection from face or voice)
Corrective action: Include in Phase 4 acceptance criteria and test cases

Requirement: Classification of AI feedback: high-risk if used to evaluate learning outcomes or steer the learning process
Source: EU AI Act Art. 6 and Annex III point 3; Art. 6(3) derogation
Applicability: To be confirmed — depends on whether AI output influences completion, assessment or certification
Evidence: Design keeps AI feedback formative and advisory; human assessor decides outcomes
Gaps: No documented classification; dates of high-risk obligations to be verified (possible postponement under EU 'digital omnibus' proposals)
Corrective action: Formal classification before Phase 4; if high-risk, implement Chapter III obligations or redesign

Requirement: Transparency: learners informed they interact with an AI system; AI-generated audio/text identifiable
Applicability: Yes once AI teachers and simulations are live
Evidence: Public pages state AI teachers are software and can make mistakes
Gaps: In-product disclosure, AI labelling of generated voices and feedback not yet built (Phase 4)
Corrective action: Build disclosure into every AI interaction; label AI-generated audio

Requirement: AI literacy of staff who operate or oversee AI systems
Source: EU AI Act Art. 4; applicable since 2 Feb 2025
Applicability: Yes once AI is deployed; prudent now
Gaps: No AI literacy training record for instructors and assessors
Corrective action: Create a short AI literacy module for staff; keep training records

Requirement: No use of learner recordings or conversations for model training without a valid basis and consent
Evidence: Privacy Policy draft states recordings are not used to train models
Gaps: Provider settings (training opt-out, retention) not configured or documented
Corrective action: Choose providers and settings that exclude training; document in the processor register

Requirement: Human oversight and transparent limitations of AI feedback
Source: EU AI Act Art. 14 (if high-risk); GDPR Art. 22; approved Academy rule
Evidence: Approved principles (AI advisory only; human final assessment); public AI note
Gaps: Not implemented in product
Corrective action: Implement human review points and a limitation notice with every AI report

Requirement: Consent before non-essential cookies or similar technologies
Source: ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3); Polish Electronic Communications Law (2024)
Evidence: Consent banner with equal 'Necessary only' and 'Accept all' options; analytics not loaded; settings can be reopened (E2E tested)
Gaps: Cookie Policy draft not reviewed; consent not recorded server-side; analytics integration (Stage 7) must read consent
Corrective action: Legal review of the policy; keep analytics consent-gated

Requirement: Prior consent for marketing emails; easy withdrawal
Source: Polish Electronic Communications Law; GDPR Art. 7
Evidence: Separate, optional, off-by-default marketing consent with history (E2E tested)
Gaps: No sending system, unsubscribe link or double opt-in yet
Corrective action: Implement unsubscribe and consent check in the email system

Requirement: Pre-contractual information for distance contracts (identity, price including taxes, main characteristics, withdrawal right)
Evidence: Pricing page shows price, inclusions and tax notice; Terms draft
Gaps: Legal entity, withdrawal information and model withdrawal form missing; checkout not built
Corrective action: Complete before taking payments; legal review

Requirement: 14-day right of withdrawal and its lawful loss for digital content/services (express consent and acknowledgement)
Source: Directive 2011/83/EU Art. 9, 16; Polish Consumer Rights Act
Evidence: Terms draft contains a placeholder
Gaps: Mixed product (digital content, digital service, live coaching) needs a specific legal structure; refund policy undefined
Corrective action: Define withdrawal and refund rules; build consent checkbox in checkout

Requirement: Conformity of digital content and services; updates
Source: Directive (EU) 2019/770; Polish Consumer Rights Act (chapter on digital content)
Gaps: Terms do not address conformity, updates or remedies
Corrective action: Add conformity and remedies section

Requirement: Fair commercial practices; no misleading claims (accreditation, outcomes, testimonials, price reductions)
Source: Directive 2005/29/EC as amended by 2019/2161; Polish Act on counteracting unfair market practices
Evidence: Manual review of all 19 public pages on 26 Nov 2026: no testimonials, statistics, accreditation or CME/CPD claims; certificate disclaimer in footer and FAQ; outcome claims qualified
Gaps: Re-verify every new page and any future discount display (30-day lowest-price rules)
Corrective action: Pre-publication marketing review checklist

Requirement: Terms of service for electronic services provided free of charge before contract
Source: Polish Act on Providing Services by Electronic Means (2002)
Evidence: /terms draft
Gaps: Required elements (technical requirements, prohibited content, complaints procedure) incomplete; legal review
Corrective action: Complete and review

Requirement: Complaints procedure
Source: Polish Consumer Rights Act; Act on Providing Services by Electronic Means
Evidence: Contact form exists
Gaps: No documented complaints procedure or response deadline
Corrective action: Adopt a Complaints and Contact Procedure

Requirement: No unjustified geo-blocking of access to services for EU customers
Applicability: To be confirmed (exception for services giving access to copyright-protected content may apply)
Evidence: No geo-restrictions implemented
Gaps: Localised pricing (Stage 7) must respect the Regulation
Corrective action: Confirm before implementing localised prices

Requirement: Digital Services Act obligations for hosting of user-submitted content
Applicability: To be confirmed — learner submissions are stored but not disseminated to the public
Gaps: Points of contact and notice-and-action not formalised
Corrective action: Legal confirmation; if applicable, publish a single point of contact and a notice mechanism

Requirement: European Accessibility Act requirements for e-commerce services
Source: Directive (EU) 2019/882; Polish implementing act (2024); applicable since 28 Jun 2025
Applicability: Probably exempt if the Academy is a microenterprise (fewer than 10 staff and annual turnover or balance sheet total ≤ EUR 2 million); applies to the purchase flow otherwise
Gaps: Enterprise size and scope not confirmed
Corrective action: Confirm status; meet WCAG 2.2 AA regardless (Academy target)

Requirement: WCAG 2.2 AA conformance (Academy target)
Type: Recommended best practice (legally required only if ACC-01 applies)
Evidence: Automated axe-core audit of 33 views (evidence/axe-2026-11-26.json); skip link; keyboard-accessible menus and dialogs; captions on sample video
Gaps: Colour contrast (186 nodes), accessible-name mismatch on logo, one scrollable region without keyboard access; no manual screen-reader audit
Corrective action: Apply the contrast and label fixes (proposed); manual NVDA/VoiceOver audit

Requirement: Accessible PDFs and learning materials
Evidence: pdfinfo: handouts and Workshop Pack report 'Tagged: no'
Gaps: PDFs untagged; no HTML alternative
Corrective action: Generate tagged PDFs with document outline; provide accessible HTML versions

Requirement: Captions and transcripts for all video and audio
Evidence: Player supports WebVTT captions (tested); sample video captioned
Gaps: No transcripts; instructor videos not yet produced (must be captioned before publication)
Corrective action: Make captions and transcripts a publication requirement

Requirement: Reasonable alternatives for learners who cannot complete voice-based exercises
Applicability: Yes (W1 and Speaking Studio rely on voice)
Gaps: No adjustment policy for speech, hearing or other impairments
Corrective action: Adopt a Reasonable Adjustments policy with alternative tasks and assessment

Requirement: Accessibility Statement
Gaps: No statement page
Corrective action: Publish after remediation and manual audit

Requirement: Rights to instructor recordings, images and likeness
Source: Polish Copyright and Related Rights Act (written transfer or licence with specified fields of exploitation; consent to distribute a person's image)
Applicability: Yes once videos and photos are produced
Evidence: No third-party media used yet
Gaps: No contributor agreements or model releases
Corrective action: Written agreements before any recording

Requirement: Licences of fonts, icons and open-source software respected
Source: SIL OFL 1.1; ISC; MIT/Apache; LGPL-3.0 (sharp/libvips); CC-BY-4.0 (caniuse-lite)
Evidence: Licence scan: 102 MIT, 7 Apache-2.0, 3 ISC, 2 0BSD, 1 BSD-3; fonts OFL; icons ISC
Gaps: No third-party notices page; LGPL and CC-BY attribution not documented
Corrective action: Publish third-party notices

Requirement: Academic citation and copyright in educational content
Evidence: Content cites sources by reference only (no reproduced figures or long quotations); pronunciation sources logged
Gaps: References not yet verified against originals by the Academic Director
Corrective action: Reference verification before launch

Requirement: Rights in learner-submitted content
Evidence: Terms draft: learners keep ownership; limited licence to process
Gaps: Not legally reviewed
Corrective action: Legal review

Requirement: Appropriate technical and organisational security measures
Evidence: RLS on all tables; 33+33 database and 23+33 API security tests; no secrets in repository (CI history scan); 0 known dependency vulnerabilities (npm audit, 26 Nov 2026)
Gaps: No HTTP security headers; no rate limiting on the contact API; no MFA for staff; no monitoring or backups configured
Corrective action: See security findings S1–S10

Requirement: Row Level Security on every table
Evidence: 15/15 public tables have RLS enabled; anonymous users only SELECT on public syllabus; automated tests in CI-ready suites
Corrective action: Keep RLS tests mandatory for every migration

Requirement: Secrets management
Evidence: No secrets in repository or history (scanner with negative test, CI); service-role key unused; .env files ignored
Corrective action: Rotate keys on staff changes; keep scanner in CI

Requirement: Backups and recovery
Gaps: Hosted database not connected; backup plan, retention and restore test undefined
Corrective action: Choose a Supabase plan with backups (consider point-in-time recovery); test restore quarterly

Requirement: Logging and monitoring
Evidence: Audit log of key account and learning events (leadership-only, tamper-resistant)
Gaps: No error monitoring, alerting or security event review
Corrective action: Add error monitoring (EU-hosted) and alerting

Requirement: Payment security
Source: PCI DSS; PSD2 strong customer authentication
Evidence: No payment processing implemented
Corrective action: Use Stripe Checkout (card data never touches the Academy); verified webhooks only

Requirement: HTTP security headers (CSP, HSTS, frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy); framework banner removed
Evidence: curl -I on 26 Nov 2026: none of the headers present; X-Powered-By: Next.js exposed
Gaps: Clickjacking and injection hardening missing
Corrective action: Add headers in next.config (CSP with nonces compatible with Supabase and future Stripe); poweredByHeader: false; test in CI

Requirement: Rate limiting and abuse protection on public endpoints (contact form, sign-up, password reset)
Evidence: Supabase Auth applies its own rate limits to sign-up, sign-in and reset emails; contact API validates input (422 on invalid)
Gaps: 20 rapid POSTs to /api/contact were all processed — no rate limit, no bot protection
Corrective action: Per-IP rate limit and a privacy-friendly challenge on the contact form before an email provider is connected

Requirement: Multi-factor authentication for staff accounts with access to learner data
Gaps: Staff use password-only sign-in
Corrective action: Require TOTP MFA (Supabase Auth MFA, aal2 checked in RLS) for all staff roles

Requirement: Secure storage of learner recordings and files (private buckets, signed URLs, size and type limits, retention)
Evidence: No learner files are stored today: W1 recordings remain on the learner's own device (stated in workshop text and facilitator guide); no storage bucket exists
Gaps: Design required before Phase 4
Corrective action: Private bucket with per-user RLS, short-lived signed URLs, malware and type checks, automated deletion

Requirement: Incident response procedure (security incidents, not only personal-data breaches)
Gaps: No roles, contacts, severity levels, key-rotation or communication plan
Corrective action: Adopt the Incident and Data Breach Response Procedure; run a tabletop exercise before launch

Requirement: Dependency and vulnerability management
Evidence: npm audit 26 Nov 2026: 0 vulnerabilities (production and development); lockfile committed; CI lint, typecheck and build
Gaps: No automated dependency updates or audit step in CI
Corrective action: Add npm audit and Dependabot (or equivalent) to CI

Requirement: Measurable learning outcomes, evidence-based content and transparent assessment
Source: Academy Content Standard; European Standards and Guidelines (ESG) principles as a reference
Evidence: Approved Content Standard; 8 of 36 items authored to standard; rubric with descriptors
Gaps: Medical expert review and reference verification not yet performed; 28 items in preparation
Corrective action: Adopt the Educational Quality Framework review workflow

Requirement: Certificate and assessment policy; no misleading accreditation
Evidence: Certificate wording and disclaimers approved; human approval required
Gaps: No published Certificate and Assessment Policy (appeals, revocation, verification privacy)
Corrective action: Publish the policy

Requirement: Stated completion and assessment rules match what the platform enforces
Source: Academy Content Standard; consumer law (accurate information)
Evidence: Platform enforces readiness check, three completed Practice Rounds and Final Task submission for W1 (database function lesson_requirements; E2E tested)
Gaps: W1 text states completion requires 'Competent in five of six criteria'; this is self-assessed and not enforced or verified by a human
Corrective action: Distinguish 'Workshop completed' (activities) from 'Assessed as Competent' (instructor review, later stage) in text and UI — see W1 Quality Gate F1

Requirement: Medical and linguistic expert review of content before publication
Evidence: Pronunciation verified against Cambridge and Oxford dictionaries (docs/curriculum/pronunciation-verification.md)
Gaps: No sign-off by a medical educator or a qualified English-language specialist recorded for any item
Corrective action: Two-reviewer sign-off with a review log per lesson

Requirement: Medical device regulation
Applicability: No — the software is intended for communication education, not for diagnosis, prevention, monitoring or treatment of patients
Evidence: Intended purpose documented; no clinical decision support
Gaps: Re-assess if any feature ever touches patient data or clinical decisions
Corrective action: Keep intended purpose statement

Requirement: UK GDPR (and UK representative) when targeting UK learners
Applicability: To be confirmed (depends on UK marketing)
Corrective action: Decide target markets; appoint representative if required

Requirement: Other national privacy laws (e.g. Switzerland FADP, US state laws, Canada)
Applicability: To be confirmed by market; most US state laws have revenue or volume thresholds unlikely to be met
Corrective action: Market-by-market review before marketing outside the EU

Requirement: VAT on cross-border sales (OSS; place of supply for electronically supplied services vs. education/virtual events); invoicing (KSeF e-invoicing in Poland)
Evidence: Pricing states taxes shown at checkout
Gaps: VAT treatment of the mixed product not determined
Corrective action: Tax opinion before Stage 7 (Stripe Tax configuration)
